expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Cowboys pivoted to a more run heavy approach the last two weeks, and it got them a big fat L against a terrible Cardinals team, so I expect them to lean back into a Dak led offense in a super cushy matchup with a tanking Colts defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb get an elite matchup against the Colts and Dake is 5th overall in the NFL with 2,046 passing yards and this is the second highest total on the slate at 51.5

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Dallas is a 5.5-point favorite in a 51.5 total, second-highest on the slate, and the Colts have been the kind of defense quarterbacks have carved up all year. Lamb gives you the stack and Tyler Warren is a cheap bring-back on the other side of a game that should go back and forth. He’s a fraction of the ownership of Purdy and Mahomes with the same kind of ceiling, and that’s the whole trade off.

players.notes: Elite matchup with high passing volume in the slate's second highest total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Week 9 is officially the week of cheap quarterbacks, and my favorite is Malik Willis. He has quietly averaged 20+ fantasy points over his last 3 games, even with the Dolphins playing one of the slowest paces in the NFL. He has also rushed for over 100 yards and 2 touchdowns in that stretch. The Lions are 29th in EPA allowed per dropback and 31st in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to quarterbacks, and Miami is a 7-point home underdog, so expect a pass-heavy approach.

players.notes: Rushing floor and pass-heavy script against a weak opposing secondary.
High implied team total and Strong passing volume as a heavy home favorite.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: The highest team total QB of the week is somehow not a top 5 owned QB on either DK or FD? That feels wrong on it's face

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: The 49ers carry the slate-high team total (30.5, up 2.5 since open) as 9.5-point home favorites against a Raiders defense that doesn’t get off the field. That’s the highest-floor spot on the board: a pass-first offense, a lead to protect, and Kittle and McCaffrey sitting at the same table so your cash lineup is correlated without trying. Nothing clever here, just the safest 20-plus on the slate.

players.notes: Leads the slate in implied team total with tremendous passing efficiency.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Miami ranks 29th in pass DVOA. Goff struggles more than most quarterbacks when he's under pressure, so having a clean pocket is especially important for him, and he should have one in this matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Dolphins have allowed over 9 yards per attempt in two straight games, a 76% completion rate in both, and numerous explosive plays.

players.notes: Clean pocket expected against a struggling secondary to maximize pass volume.
Strong passing volume and rushing upside in a competitive game total.
Attractive pass volume and Strong weapons in a solid game environment.
Value salary option with high implied team total as a heavy home favorite.
Solid passing volume expected in a narrow spread home matchup.
Favorable home favorite spot with solid passing volume and high ceiling.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Las Vegas ranks 32nd in rush DVOA, has allowed 5.31 yards per carry to running backs (most in the league), and ranks near the bottom in defensive line yards. If CMC plays (questionable with a hamstring injury), he's the top play on the slate. If he sits, we unleash Kaelon Black.

expert_blurbs.author: ebeimfohr
expert_blurbs.text: The Raiders are the saddest run defense I've seen in quite some time, and the Niners are severely lacking in weapons on offense due to injury. CMC will be popular, of course, but it's more than deserved.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Highest team total on the slate, biggest favorite on the slate, and $2,000 cheaper than Gibbs. The Raiders have been soft against the run and San Francisco should be milking the clock for a quarter, which is pure touch volume for a back who catches everything out of the backfield anyway. He’s the one piece of chalk you never fade in cash this week.

players.notes: Elite running back workload as a massive home favorite in a high total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Jahmyr Gibbs put up 28 fantasy points against the Vikings in a game where he lost snaps to Sione Vaki in pass protection. He’s been a cheat code all season, and the Dolphins are bottom 12 in EPA against the run and in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to running backs. A 25-touch day is realistic, and with all of the value at quarterback, wide receiver and tight end, he’s easy to fit.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Gibbs is expensive, but he keeps showing why he’s worth it.  I really like this Detroit game as they get an elite game environment against Miami and with the passing game options like Amon-Ra St. Brown expected to be very popular, I am looking to get overweight on Gibbs.  This is a great week to get to some elite spend up options in your lineup with all of the value pieces available to us in just about every position.

players.notes: Heavy touch volume as a workhorse against a porous run defense.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: The Chiefs are big home favorites at (9.5) and Walker now has 770 total rushing yards on the season.  He and Jahmyr Gibbs will be two of my higher-owned and higher-priced RB’s that I am targeting and I like pairing Walker with the more popular KC Chiefs defense.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Kansas City is a 10-point favorite in a 28.75 team total that moved up three points this week, which is the exact script where a lead back eats the fourth quarter. The field is funneling into McCaffrey and Gibbs at the top of the position and leaving Walker as the clear third wheel, and the Jets have had no answer for the run. He’s the pivot off the chalk backs in any lineup that wants a different game.

players.notes: Elite workhorse role as a heavy home favorite with high touchdown upside.
Strong touch projection and favorable game script as a home favorite.
Solid carry share and goal-line work in a competitive matchup.
Steady rushing volume and red-zone opportunities as a home favorite.
Exceptional pass-catching role and heavy touch volume in a close game.
Alone atop a decimated NYG RB room depth chart.
Workhorse role with heavy carry share and high red-zone conversion rate.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Washington plays soft coverage, there's no shadow corner to worry about, and Stafford should have a fairly clean pocket to work with. Washington has also allowed 33.6 fantasy points per game to wide receivers, the 12th-most in the league. It's a great matchup combined with heavy volume.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Puka Nacua is my only Core Play tag at wide receiver. He’s the top play among the expensive options, and there’s not much separating the value plays. He has a 34% target share and 39% air yards share on the season, and the target share jumps to 41% in games Davante Adams has missed. The Rams have a 26.5-point team total against the Commanders, who are 26th in EPA allowed per dropback and 21st in schedule-adjusted fantasy points allowed to wide receivers.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Washington has been one of the softer pass defenses in the league against wideouts, the Rams are 4.5-point favorites in a 48.5 total, and Nacua’s target share is the floor all by itself. He’s the engine of the Rams passing game, and the Stafford pairing is a live stack in its own right, so he’s the cash play and the GPP stack piece at the same time.

players.notes: Dominant target share and elite air yards against a soft secondary.
Elite target share and pristine route participation in a top game total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Washington is a 4.5-point home dog in a 48.5 total, which is the script where the Commanders are throwing all afternoon to keep pace with the Rams, and Williams has been the one getting the targets in that offense. At $4,100 he’s the cheapest wideout on the slate who actually matters: he’s the piece that lets you fit Gibbs and McCaffrey in the same lineup without punting somewhere else. He’s also the natural bring-back for every Stafford-Nacua stack, which is exactly where the field will be stacking.

players.notes: High target volume expected from a pass-heavy trailing game script.
Strong route participation and deep role in a close road matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: headChopper
expert_blurbs.text: Williams has been becoming a bigger part of the offense lately, and I prefer him on a touchdown-heavy site like FanDuel. I don't expect the volume to be excessive, but he's a big-play guy whose fantasy production is heavily boosted by touchdowns.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: Jameson Williams looks like a much more complete WR this year. He's getting it done downfield, finding the soft spots against zone coverage, and just has a great feel for the game right now.

expert_blurbs.author: Krayton
expert_blurbs.text: Williams has been looking like the explosive WR that we knew he was and he’s now caught 5 TD’s in the last 4 games and he is clearly becoming a bigger part of this Lions offense.  I am looking to get in my lineups more so on FD where the TD’s are very valuable and his price is very reasonable at just $6700.  He’s an elite tournament option this week.

players.notes: Explosive deep threat finding soft spots in zone coverage with high TD rate.
Steady target share and slot alignment in a pass-heavy game script.

expert_blurbs.author: DavisMattek
expert_blurbs.text: I think there is enough salary savers available across the board that playing JSN over Puka is easy enough on both DK/FD. Having Ferguson back should limit the workload a smidge for Puka and JSN has an incredible matchup against a bottom 3 EPA per play pass defense

players.notes: Elite target share and route participation as a heavy home favorite.
Deep threat role and Strong target share as a home favorite.

expert_blurbs.author: vanekjordan
expert_blurbs.text: The Browns run a ton of single-high and man coverage, and Olave is one of the best separators in the league against those looks. The Saints could also be getting multiple offensive linemen back, which should give Shough more time to take shots downfield and connect with Olave on explosive plays.

players.notes: Elite separation against man coverage with extra time from returning linemen.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: Top of the position in the 30.5 team total at $1,900 less than Bowers. The ownership is the price you pay for the highest floor at the thinnest position on the slate, and in cash that’s a feature, not a bug. Pair him with Purdy and McCaffrey and you’ve locked the whole San Francisco side of the best game environment on the board.

players.notes: Every-down route participation and elite matchup in the slate's top total.

expert_blurbs.author: BobbyGomes
expert_blurbs.text: The Raiders are 9.5-point dogs in the slate’s highest total (52, up 2.5), which means they’re being asked to throw to keep up, and Bowers is the target king in that offense. The field hates paying up at tight end on an underdog, so he comes in at a fraction of Kittle’s ownership for a comparable ceiling. He’s also the bring-back that correlates with every Purdy-McCaffrey-Kittle build on the slate.

players.notes: Target king for an underdog expected to throw constantly in a high total.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Part of me doesn’t want to chase a chalky player who wasn’t on my radar all season, and Greg Dulcich could be the highest-owned tight end this week. But he has too much going for him to fade. He has at least 5 targets in each of his last 3 games, and the Lions are dead last in fantasy points allowed to tight ends. The game script should mean plenty of dropbacks for Malik Willis, and he’s cheap.

players.notes: Consistent target volume against a defense struggling against tight ends.
Strong route participation and red-zone role in a high total.
Elite seam usage and consistent target share as a heavy home favorite.
Reliable route rate and red-zone looks in a pass-heavy script.
Massive target share and elite route rate for a trailing offense.

expert_blurbs.author: NeilCO
expert_blurbs.text: It's possible that Fannin just won't be the same star player going forward, with a lot more target competition on the Browns. But I tend to think he's actually very good, and he showed a great connection with Sanders last year. Since the start of last year, Fannin has 2.10 yards per route run (YPRR) with Sanders, and 1.67 YPRR without Sanders. Again, I acknowledge that may just be because he played with Sanders before the team drafted a couple of good rookie wide receivers. But I want to see if the connection continues to shine.

players.notes: Strong yards per route run and proven connection with the quarterback.
Solid route participation and red-zone role in a competitive matchup.

expert_blurbs.author: Notorious
expert_blurbs.text: Just because Shedeur Sanders is one of my favorite value plays doesn’t mean I can’t like the Saints D/ST. They’re coming off a bye and playing at home against a turnover-prone quarterback. If the offense plays better than it has lately, New Orleans should build a lead. That would mean 35+ dropbacks for Sanders, and I expect sacks and mistakes. They’re also cheap on both sites.
